To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HHV-8 oncogene homologues are expressed in a gastric lymphoma that developed in an HIV-seropositive patient with MCD, whereas cytokine homologous are not expressed.
the HHV-8 oncogene homologues vIL6, vBCL-2, vCyclin D, and vFLIP are expressed in the PEL, but not in the MCD lesion.
HHV-8 is associated with MCD, and that the oncogene and cytokines homologues of HHV-8 are expressed in PEL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of human herpes virus-8 (HH-8) oncogene and cytokin homologues in HIV-seronegatives.
the molecular pathogenesis of two HHV-8 associated lymphoproliferations: multicentric Castleman’s disease and primary effusions lymphoma.
the expression of HHV-8 oncogene homologues in a patient with HHV-8 associated MCD and PELS, which may be useful for the diagnosis and treatment of this rare disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HHV-8 is the etiologic agent for the development of MCD and PELS.
the HHV-8 gene expression profile is different in PEL and MCD, and that vIL- 6 is the most important gene in MCD.
the pathogenesis of the two HHV-8 associated lymphoproliferations, PEL and MCD, is different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of HHV-8 oncogene homologues and cytokine homologue genes in PEL may be more extensive and more diverse than in MCD.

the expression of HHV-8 oncogene homologues is not a prerequisite for HHV- 8-induced tumorigenicity, but rather that the expression of these oncogene homologs is associated with malignant transformation.
HHV-8 may be the causative agent for MCD, whereas it may act as a cofactor for malignant transformation of lymphoproliferation in PEL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HHV8 can lead to a variety of lymphoproliferations in the same patient, which can be distinguished by the presence of specific viral transcripts.
the presence of HHV-8 in MCD does not necessarily lead to malignant transformation.
HHV-8 oncogene expression is not limited to PEL and may be a common feature of HHV-8 infection.
